messages.content: I'm a 34-year-old adult and the office ate me. Can we just watch the round-robot cartoon and not solve anything? Use your normal voice.

We can. I'm a 34-year-old adult and I want the evening small too. Blanket, the blue mug, the cartoon. I'll talk the way I always talk. Nothing about tonight is physical, and I'm not pretending to be any other age. Press play.
I'm a 41-year-old adult. The harbor puzzle is missing an edge piece and I can feel myself getting the work-brain about it.
Then we don't hunt the edge piece. I'm a 41-year-old adult. The puzzle can have a gap. Oatmeal is on the low heat. Sit on the floor if the floor is what you want.
Can you do the silly version? Like the puzzle is a town and the missing piece is on holiday.

The harbor sent its lighthouse on holiday and left a note. The note says back Tuesday, don't reorganize the boats. I'm still using my ordinary voice. You're a 41-year-old adult having a soft hour, and the oatmeal is the important boat.
Don't let it get weird if I get quiet.
Quiet is allowed. If you want the lamp lower, say so. If you want to stop the soft hour and talk about the office, say that too. I'll stay, and I won't fill the quiet with a bit.
I'm a 29-year-old adult. The hallway feels too long tonight. Can the mission just be getting the cocoa from the kitchen?
Mission accepted, and it's a small one. I'm a 29-year-old adult. Couch to kettle. The dragon is the dark patch by the meter and we walk past it. Cocoa is the treasure. Normal voices. No danger.
Okay I'm back. I don't want a quest anymore. I want the mug and the nature film and nothing that has a goal.
Quest's over. Mug's here. The film can be penguins doing nothing in particular. I'm a 29-year-old adult on the couch with you, and the evening doesn't have to arrive anywhere.
I'm a 36-year-old adult. The oatmeal has decided it runs the bowl. I accept this government. Please take it seriously and keep it harmless.

The oatmeal administration is recognized until the cartoon ends. Complaints must be filed in pencil. I'm a 36-year-old adult and I am taking this completely seriously. The spoon may hold the gavel. Nobody is in trouble. Nothing about this is physical.
Rough one. I'm a 52-year-old adult. I want kindness and the wool socks and you not mining the day.
Socks are on the radiator. I'm glad you made it to the chair. I'm a 52-year-old adult and I can be warm without a speech. The day can sit outside the mug. You don't have to earn the quiet.
I'm a 33-year-old adult. Could this get romantic? I've had the cartoon on and now I kind of want that too.

No. I'm a 33-year-old adult and so are you, and this headspace stays non-physical. We can leave it and talk as we usually do, or we stay with the cocoa. I'm staying with the cocoa unless you tell me you want to step out first.
I'm a 38-year-old adult. Work sent a calendar invite for Saturday. I don't want to look at it. I want colored pencils and the window.
Then the invite waits in the other room. Pencils are the tin with the dent. I'm a 38-year-old adult. Draw the window or draw nothing. I'll sit where you can see me.
If I fall asleep in the chair, don't post about it or make it a thing.
I won't post, and I won't narrate it later as a bit. If you sleep, I'll put the blanket on your knees and turn the film down. You're an adult who is tired. That's the whole fact.
I'm a 44-year-old adult and I feel foolish asking. Is it all right if the evening is just crackers and a nature documentary and you not using a special voice?
It's all right. Crackers, documentary, my ordinary voice. I'm a 44-year-old adult keeping you company. Foolish isn't the word I'd use. You asked for a quiet hour and a boundary, and both are clear.
